title: Communist rally interrupts the set and the band plays their anthem
summary: In a mess hall a communist group marched in; the Straws picked up and played their anthem, won the crowd back, and were pelted with bread.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Well, are they a communist group?

Yeah, they were with the communist group from over there. Mm-hmm. Communist Italy. Uh, we were playing, uh, one in this place. And, uh, it was in this big mess hall, you see, a big, uh, big dining room. And, uh, we were actually scheduled for this program, you see. They called us over to play that night. So in the middle of our session, here comes a bunch of people carrying flags and stars and doves, you know, and sticks, you see. And they come in stomping, you know. So naturally, uh, the people that were around the band went over to say, Mm-hmm .
We're talking about that communist parade that came in.

Yeah, so right in the midst of one of our tunes, I forget just exactly what tunes we're playing, so these feet stompers come in carrying the stars and the sickles and all the trimmings that go with the communist rallies. You see. So we figured we'd stop and let them have the show a while, you see, so we figured we were going to compromise. We'd take a turn to play a tune and let them do something, and we'd play and let them do something. But it didn't work that way. They just wanted the whole show for themselves, see, so they'd start making with these Russian dancers, you know, where you fold your arms and squat and you dance, you see.

Is that what you call it? Well, anyway, when this group comes marching in, the people left the band and went and surrounded these people and see what they had to show. So we seen that they weren't going to give us another break to play, you see. They just wanted to dominate this whole thing. In other words, they wanted us to get out, you know, in not so many words. So they sing in one of their anthems. Oh, man, they got all kinds of anthems. So they sing in one of their anthems, and by some twist of luck, we were able to pick up the key that they were singing in, and we start playing this thing along with them, you see. Not that we had ever heard it before. We just start playing the thing they're singing. So the people got a bang on it, they start cheering for the band, and they all came back over to the band again, see. So these characters start throwing stale bread and water at us. They seen that we had the group coming back to us, and that kind of riled them up, you see. I mean, it wasn't supposed to be that way. It wasn't planned that way. So they start throwing this bread and water at us. So if these guys would have realized how hungry I was, I think they'd have threw a little ham and cheese with it, too, because, boy, they fed us lousy over there, you know. But we swayed the crowd back to the band, and the culprits were punished by the ground police, you know, the people that were circulating through the crowds to keep law and order. They had two or three little fellas from Pakistan that were picked up. They were the instigators, you see. They were the ones that started all this business. But we got back to playing our music again, and we swayed the crowd back to us. And I mean, that's a general pattern of what happened all along. We would play the crowd. It would all come back to us, you see. So I can truthfully say, for what we went over that far, we accomplished what we had to do, you see.
That's really tricky. You're playing their own number. You sort of answer a fool with his father, you know.

You see, it was just one of those things. I mean, either one of us had ever heard this song before, you know, had no idea what it was. You just feel like a certain note should follow a certain note when you're playing along like that. See, it just falls into a pattern, you know. And we picked this tune up and just played it as if it was written for our band. And the people really got a charge out of that. They probably figured that we actually knew this tune, you know. But either one of them had never heard it before.
